#### Cycle 1 ligations

To a solution of each FKBP ligand-connector DNA conjugate (30 nmol, 66 μL, 1.5 eq) was added 10x T4 ligase buffer (Lucigen, 20 μL), pre-annealed forward primer binding site oligo (1 mM in dH2O, 20 μL, 20 nmol, 1 eq), a unique cycle 1 tag (1 mM in dH2O, 44 μL, 44 nmol, 2.2 eq), and T4 DNA Ligase (Lucigen, 30 Weiss U / μL, 0.8 μL, 24 Weiss U / ligation). Each ligation was incubated overnight at room temperature. Reaction completion was assessed by running an analytical sample of each ligation reaction on a 4% agarose gel (E-gel EX 4%). The ligations were pooled in a 50mL Falcon tube, and subjected to ethanol precipitation.

#### Ns deprotection

To a 0.1 mM solution of the pooled FKBP ligand-connector DNA conjugate 5 (860 nmol ligated with cycle 1 tags, 1290 nmol, 1.0 eq total DNA conjugates) in bicarbonate buffer (pH 10) was added 4-methoxy thiophenol (1.29 mmol, 1000 eq, 100mM in DMF). Reaction was incubated at 80 °C for 2 hours. After cooling to rt, the products were subjected to ethanol precipitation.

#### Cycle 2 ligations

440 nmol of the deprotected Cycle 1 ligations were dissolved in 570uL of water and split across 290 wells using 96-well plates (2 uL, 1.52 nmol). To each well was added a unique cycle 2 tag (2.3 μL, 1 mM solution in dH2O, 3.34 nmol, 2.2 eq) followed by a mixture of T4 DNA ligase and 5x ligase buffer (3.75 μL, 1.85 Weiss U / well) for a final volume of 10 μL per ligation. The ligations were incubated at RT overnight. The reactions were precipitated with the addition of 1 μL of 5 M NaCl and 100 μL of ice-cold ethanol. Plates were incubated at −20°C for 1 h and the pellets were isolated by centrifugation. The supernatant was carefully decanted and the pellets were washed with an additional 100 μL of ice-cold ethanol and then air-dried for 1 h.

#### Connector amine substitution with triazine and further SNAr with 290 cycle 2 amines

Each of the 290 wells from the above cycle 2 ligations was dissolved in a mixture of 10 μL water, 10 μL pH 8 PBS buffer, and 15.45 μL MeCN, and was cooled to 4°C in a thermocycler. Cyanuric chloride (4.55 μL of 3 mM solution in MeCN, 20 eq) was added and incubated at 4 °C overnight. The following day, additional cyanuric chloride (4.55 μL of 3 mM solution in MeCN, 20 eq) was added. After additional 5 hours at 4°C, each well received one of 290 amines (200 mM in 1:1 MeCN:dH2O, 2.275 μL, 200 eq). The reactions were maintained at 4°C overnight. The reactions were pooled, and each well was rinsed with an additional 15 μL water. The combined reaction was then subjected to ethanol precipitation.

#### Ligation of cycle 3 tags for encoding of 249 final triazine substitutions

The pooled material from cycle 2 was split across 249 wells (1.77 nmol, 1 eq). A unique cycle 3 tag (4.16 μL, 1 mM solution in dH2O, 4.16 nmol, 2.35 eq) was added to each well, followed by a freshly prepared solution of T4 DNA ligase in 5x ligase buffer (4.4 μL, 2.1 Weiss U / well) to give a final volume of 10 μL per well. The plates were briefly spun down and incubated at RT overnight. The reaction wells were then subjected to DNA precipitation.

#### Final substitution of triazine with 249 cycle 3 amines

To each of the 249 wells from the above cycle 3 ligations (1.77 nmol, 26.6 μL PBS pH 8 buffer, 1 eq) was added one of 249 amines (200 mM in 1:1 CH3CN:dH2O, 2.66 μL, 532 nmol, 300 eq). The reaction plates were sealed and heated to 80°C for 16 h. The resulting reactions were pooled and each well rinsed with 15 μL water. The combined reactions were then subjected to ethanol precipitation.

#### Closing tag ligation

The CIP-DEL library synthesis was completed with the addition of a closing DNA segment containing a double-stranded 10 bp library tag, a single-stranded 12 nucleotide unique molecular identifier (UMI), and a single-stranded 20 nucleotide closing primer binding site. Approximately 220 nmol (375 μL in water, 1.0 eq) of the crude library was closed by adding the closing tags containing the library tag and the reverse primer binding site (400 μL, 800 nmol, 0.2 mM solution in dH2O, 3.6 eq), and a solution of T4 DNA ligase in 5x ligase buffer (300 μL, 147.6 Weiss U). The ligation mixture was gently vortexed, spun down, and incubated at room temperature overnight. The final reaction mixture was subjected to ethanol precipitation.

#### Purification by Preparative continuous flow electrophoresis

A Bio-Rad Model 491 Prep Cell was used according to manufacturer guidelines to purify crude DNA-encoded libraries following the ligation of oligonucleotides bearing a closing primer-binding site sequence. The gel assembly tube (small or large) was cast with 4% agarose in 1 × TBE buffer to a height of 8.5–9.5 cm and left to solidify over 2 h while circulating rt water through the cooling core at approx. 100 mL/min, carefully overlaying 2 mL of a 1:1 mixture of IPA and water on the top of the gel, then standing overnight at rt without water circulation through the cooling core. After standard assembly of the Prep Cell (see: http://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/M1702925.pdf) and addition of 1 × TBE buffer, the crude DEL sample was loaded in Novex™ Hi-Density TBE Sample Buffer (5X, Invitrogen LC6678), and electrophoresis was run at 12 W constant power. Fraction collection was performed using a Masterflex L/S easy-load II (Cole Parmer, 77200-50) running at approx 1 mL/min and BioFrac™ fraction collector (Bio-Rad) with a fraction time window of 2 min, i.e., (approx 2 mL fractions). Total electrophoresis time was roughly 3.5 h. Fractions were analyzed by E-GEL Power Snap device (Invitrogen, G8100) using commercial gels (Invitrogen, E-Gel EX, 4% agarose). Product-containing fractions of adequate purity were pooled, then concentrated/desalted using Millipore Amicon Ultra-15/4 centrifugal filters; Ultracel 10 K according to manufacturer’s guidelines, washing at least twice with nuclease-free water. Final yield = 50.5 nmol, 23%.
